research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent second-half minus first-half (H2-H1) change
half-to-half scoring change as a team-level trait
persistence and reliability of defensive effects across seasons
regression to the mean in team-season defensive effects
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change repeatable across seasons (cross-season or split-sample reliability) rather than noise?
What reliability and sample size are needed to detect a stable defensive H2-H1 effect with 120 team-seasons?
How are defensive effects separated from opponent quality, pace, score state and regression to the mean?
Does a residualized trait survive a placebo (shuffled half labels) and a permutation null?

historical_evidence.finding: A1 adaptation falsification study. The apparent adapter PPP lift (+0.0667, n=205) was not separated from no-signal (+0.1260) or wrong-way (+0.0111) teams in the recorded tests. Next-game carryover was null (Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842). Failure mechanism recorded as C_artifact; limitations recorded as label/classification error and selection or regression to the mean.

Defensive scheme change within and across games used inferred labels. Change rates were high (within-game 61.0%, cross-game 67.7%; 103/104 units show a change) and transition matrices were near-uniform. The record states the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently, and that near-uniform matrices are consistent with label noise.
Superstar suppression profiles. Rank-1 suppressor deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE, with no multiple-comparison control; verdict recorded as 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'.

Sequential suppression of stars by preceding opponent play type. PUTBACK was the top suppressor for 6+ stars, with n_after between 32 and 95 in several cells. Recorded as having no multiplicity correction; validation not recorded.

Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, regular season vs playoffs, for 25 teams (min 30 possessions per cell). DRIVE PPP allowed fell 1.191 to 0.923. A +12.1pp PNR share jump may reflect tagging differences. No inferential test was run.
Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency in H2 trigger games across 55 series. Team AVOID% ranged from 50.6% (ORL) to 6.8% (SAC). The record reports no outcome test; player samples were 10-178 possessions.

Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap for initiators: pooled gap +0.427 in the same direction as the team gap. Only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. Status is recorded as supported; the sample-size limitation is noted in the record.

Play-type replacement similarity vs absorb/cascade when a player sits. Similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (mean +0.863 vs +0.848; Spearman -0.19, wrong-signed). Recorded as a null with failure type B_powered_null, though sample and power were recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a defensive adaptation effect on PPP using a no-signal comparison and next-game carryover
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact. The apparent lift did not survive the asymmetry and carryover tests. Recorded limitations were label/classification error and selection or regression to the mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring defensive scheme labels from play data to measure within-game and cross-game defensive change
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable. The inferred label cannot separate defensive adjustment from offensive variation, and near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking star suppressors across many lineup, defender and play-type cells
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear. Deltas were mostly within 1-2 SE and there was no multiple-comparison control.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequential suppression by preceding opponent play type, read as individual star suppressors
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear. No multiplicity correction, and several cells had n_after of only 32-95.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using play-type replacement similarity to separate absorption from cascade
failed_approaches.why: The effect was wrong-signed and null (Spearman -0.19). Sample and power were recorded as NOT_RECORDED, so the null's informativeness is unverified.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing defensive PPP and share by play type between regular season and playoffs
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with no inferential test. A large share jump may reflect tagging differences, and the sample was 25 teams.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests whether a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait. The retrieved set does not address the question as posed.

Earlier work from this project on defensive and star-level suppression, play-type tiers and scheme labels has repeatedly been descriptive, inconclusive or artifactual when it lacked multiplicity control, placebo checks or adequate sample sizes (e.g., FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-050, FAM:SF-APPA-001).

Inferred labels derived from play-by-play (scheme labels, play-type tags) carry a recorded label-error risk that has undermined earlier conclusions (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-APPS-012).
Small per-player or per-cell samples were a recorded limitation in several earlier families (FAM:SF-APPS-036, FAM:SF-APPS-015, FAM:SF-APPA-050).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether team-season defensive H2-H1 effects are stable across seasons. No retrieved record measures cross-season or split-half reliability of this quantity.
The size of regression to the mean for H2-H1 defensive effects, or the sample needed to detect them.
Whether score state, garbage time, pace, fatigue or opponent quality confound H2-H1 defensive measures.

Whether the persistence result FAM:SF17 (supported) transfers to defense. That record concerns offensive association structure across split halves, not defensive H2-H1 change, so it is not direct evidence here.
Whether the playoff-versus-regular-season differences in FAM:SF-APPS-012 generalize to H2-H1 reliability.
own_inferences: The 120 team-seasons are likely 30 teams across four seasons (2022-23 to 2025-26), counting the partial 2025-26 data if used. Cross-season pairs per lag would be about 90, which is small for reliability estimation.

Each team-season's H2-H1 opponent change is a difference of two noisy half-level means, so its noise is roughly double that of a single-half mean. Reliability is likely low unless the true between-team variance is large.
Score state is a likely confounder: leading teams substitute bench players and change tempo in H2, which affects opponents' H2-H1 PPP without any defensive cause.
A defensive trait that is absorbed into opponent quality or pace would look reliable without being a defensive effect. Residualization is required before any reliability claim.

The prior project pattern (play-type tiers and star suppressors that did not survive multiplicity control or placebo checks) suggests that any positive result from a flexible specification is at high risk of being an artifact.
uncertainties: The retrieval returned no record that defines or measures defensive H2-H1 change; the mapping from the retrieved records to this question is inferred, not stated.
Whether the 2025-26 season data are complete at the decision date (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21) is not confirmed for every unit.
Exact possession counts per team-season per half are not in the retrieved records; the noise estimate is an inference.
Some retrieved records show NOT_RECORDED for validation, sample and power, or notes; their status cannot be checked.
Whether H2 is defined as second half of regulation, and whether overtime and garbage time are excluded, is not specified in the task and changes the estimand.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved history did not answer the question, but it changed the design. It showed that earlier work from this project on defensive and star-level effects, and on inferred labels, was descriptive, inconclusive or artifactual, mainly because of missing multiplicity control, missing placebo checks, small cells and label noise. The plan therefore fixes the estimand, residualizes score state, pace and opponent quality before any reliability claim, requires a placebo and a permutation null, and adds an explicit power rule. It also treats the 120-unit sample as likely underpowered for a reliability claim, which moves the decision from a plain proceed to proceed_with_changes.

blocking_constraints.text: A team-season H2-H1 opponent-change measure has high noise from two half-level means and an unknown split-half reliability. The reliability cannot be estimated without a validated measure.
With 120 team-seasons (about 90 cross-season pairs), power to detect a modest reliability correlation is limited. Only fairly large trait variance would be detectable.
Score state, garbage-time substitution, pace and opponent quality can produce H2-H1 differences that look like defensive traits.
Selecting teams or seasons by extreme H1 or H2 values produces regression to the mean and inflates apparent persistence.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait. Related earlier work covers defensive PPP by regular season versus playoffs (descriptive), star and defensive suppression (inconclusive or not hypothesis tests, without multiplicity control), defensive scheme labels (untestable, label noise), and an adaptation test (artifact, with regression to the mean and label error). FAM:SF17 is supported but concerns offensive association structure, not defense. The earlier work supplies cautionary precedent, not an answer.

risks.text: Split-half and cross-season reliability of the H2-H1 defensive measure is unknown and may be low given the noise of two half-level means.
120 team-seasons give limited power for a reliability correlation; the minimum detectable correlation must be stated before analysis.
Score state (leading teams and bench use in H2), pace, fatigue and opponent quality can drive H2-H1 differences without a defensive cause.
Selecting extreme team-seasons on H1 or H2 values produces regression to the mean and inflated apparent persistence.
Possession and play-type tags are inferred. Mislabelled tags (cf. FAM:SF-APPS-012 PNR share jump, FAM:SF-APPA-005 near-uniform matrices) can create spurious defensive differences.
Flexible choices of half definition, residualization and play-type split multiply the chance of a positive result (cf. FAM:SF-APPM-022, FAM:SF-APPA-050).
A positive result without a shuffled-half or placebo-period check could reflect structure in the schedule or substitution pattern rather than a defensive effect (cf. FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Rule and league-wide scoring changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can shift H2-H1 means, so cross-season persistence may partly reflect league-level drift.
If the true between-team variance is small, a null result is the likely outcome, and an adequately powered null is a legitimate conclusion.

design.estimand: Team-level defensive effect on opponents' H2-H1 change in opponent PPP, residualized for score margin, garbage time, pace and opponent quality, and its stability across seasons (cross-season correlation and ICC of the residualized trait).
design.unit: Team-season (defending team, season, regular season; playoffs analysed separately).
design.sample: 120 team-seasons (30 teams x 4 seasons, 2022-23 to 2025-26), regular season only for the primary test. Use only complete seasons; 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs from the primary test. Overtime and garbage-time possessions are excluded by a pre-specified margin rule.
design.power: Before analysis, compute the minimum detectable cross-season correlation at alpha 0.05 with about 90 adjacent-season pairs and state it. Proceed only if the minimum detectable correlation is at or below the pre-registered effect size of interest (e.g., r=0.25). If not, report the question as underpowered rather than testing it.
design.controls: Residualize opponent H2-H1 PPP on H1 level (to address RTM), score margin at half, garbage-time share, pace, opponent quality (prior-season net rating) and tagging-quality indicators. Estimate reliability using odd-versus-even game splits within season and across adjacent seasons, with empirical-Bayes shrinkage. Use pre-registered residualization; do not choose covariates after seeing results.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo: shuffle half labels within game and recompute the trait; the observed reliability must exceed the 95th percentile of the placebo distribution. (b) Permutation: permute team labels within season to build a null for cross-season correlation. (c) Test whether the residualized trait is explained by opponent quality or pace alone. The hypothesis is falsified if the residualized reliability does not exceed the permutation and placebo nulls.
design.multiplicity: One primary test (residualized cross-season ICC/correlation for regular season). Secondary analyses (playoffs, alternative half definitions, play-type splits) are exploratory and reported as such, with Holm correction across the secondary family.
design.decision_rule: Call the trait reliable only if the primary residualized cross-season correlation (or ICC) has a 95% bootstrap lower bound above 0 and exceeds the permutation and placebo 95th percentiles, with the minimum detectable effect pre-registered and met. Otherwise report a null or inconclusive result, and do not describe the trait as established.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season (play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, box-score summary), versions frozen and hashed at the decision date (2026-10-06). Derived play-type graph records are not used for the primary test because their tagging is a recorded label-error risk. 2025-26 playoffs are excluded from the primary test.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
